fresh_retrievals.source_citation: Liddell, Henry George; Scott, Robert; Jones, Henry Stuart (1940). A Greek-English Lexicon, s.v. καυνάκης (Perseus Digital Library digital edition)

fresh_retrievals.source_locator: LSJ 1940, entry καυνάκης (headword line and etymology parenthetical)
fresh_retrievals.source_excerpt: καυνάκης [α^], ου, ὁ, thick cloak, Ar.V.1137; "κ. πορφυροῦς" Men.972; said to be of Persian or Babylonian make, Arr.An.6.29.5, Poll.7.59, cf. Sch.Ar.l.c., Semus 20, PCair.Zen.48.3 (iii B.C.), PHib.1.121.11 (iii B.C.):—also καυνάκη, ἡ, PSI 6.605 (iii B.C.); cf. γαυνάκη (which is also found in codd. of Peripl.M.Rubr.6):—Dim. καυνάκιον, τό, Zonar. (Assyr. gaunakka 'frilled and flounced mantle'.)
fresh_retrievals.supports: The label is a Greek word glossed 'thick cloak', 'said to be of Persian or Babylonian make', cited to Greek primary texts (Aristophanes Wasps 1137; Menander fr. 972; Arrian Anabasis 6.29.5; Pollux 7.59) and to dated 3rd-century BC papyri (PCair.Zen.48.3; PHib.1.121.11; PSI 6.605). LSJ's own etymology parenthetical ('Assyr. gaunakka') disagrees in kind with CAD's 'foreign word' + 'possible connection' (see R8-F02-P1) — lexicographic disagreement recorded, not resolved.
fresh_retrievals.limits: The LSJ-cited papyri and Menander fragment were not themselves retrieved (papyri.info bot-walled this round); they stand as citations, not passage support.

fresh_retrievals.source_excerpt: 1137 οἱ μὲν καλοῦσι Περσίδ' οἱ δὲ καυνάκην. | 1143 οὔκ, ἀλλ' ἐν Ἐκβατάνοισι ταῦθ' ὑφαίνεται. | 1147-1149 αὕτη γέ τοι ἐρίων τάλαντον καταπέπωκε ῥᾳδίως. ... οὔκουν ἐριώλην δῆτ' ἐχρῆν αὐτὴν καλεῖν δικαιότερον ἢ καυνάκην;
fresh_retrievals.worker_literal_gloss: 1137 'Some call it a Persian robe, others a kaunakes.' | 1143 'No, but these are woven in Ecbatana.' | 1147-1149 'this one has easily swallowed down a talent of wool ... should it not be called a wool-snatcher rather than a kaunakes?' — worker gloss, not a published translation.

fresh_retrievals.source_citation: Jaramago, Miguel (2023). 'Un orante sumerio en el Museo Arqueológico Nacional (Madrid)', Boletín del Museo Arqueológico Nacional 42/2023, pp. 465-484, ISSN 2341-3409, CC BY 4.0; footnote 26 (p. 469)
fresh_retrievals.retrieval_method: FetchURL of the journal PDF (author's text and footnotes extracted)
fresh_retrievals.source_locator: footnote 26, p. 469 (article pp. 465-484); quoted authors inside it: Heuzey (via Przyluski 1931:341), Przyluski, Kawami 2018:675, Breniquet 2013:5, Breniquet 2016:9 (Durand's Mari terminology), CAD vol. 5 p. 134
fresh_retrievals.source_excerpt: El término kaunakes, usado en la literatura griega, habría sido (según Heuzey) «emprunté par les Grecs aux langues asiatiques pour désigner une étoffe chaldéenne»; se desconoce su nombre original (véase gunakku en el Chicago Assyrian Dictionary, 1956: vol. 5, 134, sub voce). ... En Kawami (2018:675) se describe el kaunakes como «horizontal rows of long flounces or perhaps lappets, with slightly pointed ends». Breniquet (2013:5) afirma que no es posible identificar con seguridad el material en que estaba hecho: «it would thus seem that this clothing is made up of a woven base or net onto which the finishing details are attached». En cuanto al término sumerio o acadio para denominar esta prenda, nos es desconocido, aunque Breniquet (2016:9) apunta que «dans la terminologie paléo-babylonienne de Mari examinée par J.M. Durand, le terme aguhhum pourrait désigner un textile tissé (et non un simple vêtement) avec de longues mèches de laine, Ce vêtement semble "démodé" à l'époque des textes de Mari et réservé à des usages liturgiques désuets».
fresh_retrievals.supports: (i) 'the Sumerian or Akkadian term for this garment is unknown' — the naming-vs-native-term separation stated in a peer-reviewed article; (ii) the Greek term is described as borrowed, with the original name unknown, and the article independently cites CAD vol. 5 p. 134 s.v. gunakku, matching R8-F02-P1; (iii) Breniquet 2013:5 is quoted that the material 'cannot be securely identified'; (iv) Breniquet 2016:9 offers only a hedged native candidate (aguhhum, Old Babylonian Mari terminology per Durand) and calls the garment archaic/liturgical; (v) Kawami 2018:675 describes the pictured texture as 'long flounces or perhaps lappets' — hedged form description, not fibre.
fresh_retrievals.support_scope: passage-level (mediated scholarly quotations with named pages); Breniquet's own article text was NOT retrieved this round (see access_failures), so these are second-hand quotations, not first-hand article passages
fresh_retrievals.limits: The article is a museum-object study; the Breniquet/Kawami quotations are reproduced from it, page-referenced but not collated against the originals.
